Hi Morgan — thanks for the heads up and the usage extract. We can do both of the things you asked, there are a couple practical options depending on how you want to amortize cost vs. keep invoice timing simple. High-level options:

1) Pro-rata immediate top-up (single invoice)
   - One-time invoice for the remaining term pro-rated to your Mar 15 renewal.
   - No financing; discount remains as per current tiering.

2) Staged uplift with split-billing (preferred for smoothing)
   - We can split the uplift into 2 or 3 equal invoices across the remainder of the term.
   - We offer a small financing allowance for staged payments (we typically apply a 2.5% fee on the financed portion).

3) Blended co-term + capacity voucher
   - If you want to annualize now and co-term immediately, we can annualize the added capacity into the renewal and apply a 5% structured uplift credit during the first quarter post-renewal.

Immediate next steps I suggest:
- If you want staged billing, confirm # of installments (2 vs 3).
- Ben & Rishi, can you confirm internal approval to surface the 2.5% financing fee and whether we can stretch it to 90 days?

I’ll draft a short amendment and a pro-forma invoice once we align.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Lead, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Stratum uplift options (PRICING)

Ben / Rishi — quick internal note before I respond to Morgan’s procurement:

Context: Stratum wants ~40% more capacity for the next 3.5 months (through Mar 15 renewal). They prefer split billing across 2 cycles.

Proposal we can offer (call these A/B):
A) Two-installment staged uplift (preferred by customer)
   - Add 40% additional capacity, billed as two equal invoices on Dec 15 and Jan 15.
   - Financing fee: 2.5% on uplift (applies only if installments > 1).
   - Discount: keep current renewal discount band (no extra midterm discount), but include 30-day early-renewal credit if they commit to +12 months at renewal.

B) Single pro-rata top-up
   - One invoice for pro-rated remainder (no financing fee).
   - Offer small one-time credit (1.5%) for immediate payment to keep cash flow neutral.

Margins: both options preserve acceptable unit economics given current model mix; staged uplift introduces low credit risk.

If you’re ok with 2.5% fee we’ll present A as the recommended path; otherwise push B with the 1.5% payment discount.

Also: I will attach the draft amendment and a pro-forma invoice for Morgan tomorrow.

Thanks,
Naomi
